hero.name: Daniel Gaio
hero.headline: Software, data and AI, built around practical problems.
hero.summary: I’m a computer engineer with experience in software for financial services, automation and applied AI. Here I bring together the things I build, the decisions behind them and what I’m learning along the way.

story.heading: From understanding a problem to building a useful solution
paragraphs: My path connects computer engineering with software and automation in financial services. Across these experiences, I’ve worked with backend APIs, data integration, production support and technical documentation.

ProsperSync is where I explore a product of my own: a personal finance application that combines expense capture from images and voice with conversational financial insights. Building it also means connecting AI services to the product and working on shared configuration and delivery automation.

This website is my next learning project. I’m building it with TypeScript, Node.js and AWS, with practical exercises in security, reliability, observability and distributed systems. I want to show the decisions, tradeoffs and lessons as the work develops.

items.title: ProsperSync: from an image or voice note to an expense
items.summary: Building the expense-capture experience of a personal finance application, using images and voice as inputs. This work brings together the Next.js application, PostgreSQL and OpenAI.

items.title: ProsperSync: connecting AI analysis to the product
items.context: Personal project · Backend integration and delivery
items.summary: Built a financial-analysis service with Python, FastAPI and LangGraph, with shared model configuration and provider integration. Delivery work also includes automation for application-function deployments and database migrations.
items.detailPrompt: Develop a case study around the service boundary, configuration choices and delivery workflow, using shareable examples and observed results.

learning.heading: Learning by building on AWS
learning.summary: This website is an AWS learning project as well as a portfolio. Planned exercises will cover private origins, cache behavior, release recovery and observability, with their costs and cleanup recorded.
learning.status: In progress; the new website has not launched on AWS yet.
